starter: Greet learners with a creative warm-up clap / body percussion.
Show picture charts and real artworks linked to today's lesson; ask 'What can you see? How does it make you feel?'

NEW TODAY (Week 1): Creative Arts – we study some visual artworks created by Ghanaian and other African visual artists living in Africa and examine how the artworks reflect the history and culture of the people in Africa Learners are to
Introduce tools/materials and safety rules for handling them.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Demonstration – 5 min): Teacher models the skill using picture charts and real artworks – study some visual artworks created by Ghanaian and other African visual artists living in Africa and examine how the artworks reflect the history and culture of the people in Africa Learners are to

plenary: Clean-up song – pupils tidy tools and materials together.

Preview next Visual/Performing Arts lesson.

sessionTitle: Weekly Reading Period — A folk tale book
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to: read independently for pleasure and information, and keep a reading log.
competencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Communication and Collaboration; Creativity and Innovation; Personal Development and Leadership; Cultural Identity and Global Citizenship; Digital Literacy
resources: NaCCA approved textbook; TLMs; ICT tools; community resources
rpk: Learners can hold simple conversations, read short passages and write structured sentences and paragraphs from Basic 1-4.
starter: Greet learners; 1-minute 'book talk': teacher shows and names a book from the class collection.
Quick recall: learners mention one thing they read last time.
NEW TODAY: Everyone reads a folk tale book quietly.
Set reading rules: eyes on text, quiet lips, note new words.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Silent reading – 7 min): Learners read a folk tale book individually; teacher listens to 2-3 learners read aloud in turn.
ACTIVITY 2 (Pair read – 5 min): Pairs take turns reading short passages aloud to each other; partners help with hard words.
ACTIVITY 3 (Respond to text – 5 min): Learners answer 3 quick questions: 'What was it about? Who was in it? Which part did you like?'
ACTIVITY 4 (Record – 3 min): Learners write the title and one sentence about a folk tale book in their reading log.
plenary: 2-3 learners share their favourite part with the class.
Teacher displays the reading log and praises consistent readers.
Homework: read one page to a family member and retell it.
Encourage learners to borrow a book for the week.
assessment: Class exercises; oral questions; practical performance; SBA

starter: Greet learners; 1-minute 'book talk': teacher shows and names a book from the class collection.

NEW TODAY: Everyone reads a short story book quietly.
Set reading rules: eyes on text, quiet lips, note new words.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Silent reading – 7 min): Learners read a short story book individually; teacher listens to 2-3 learners read aloud in turn.

plenary: 2-3 learners share their favourite part with the class.
Teacher displays the reading log and praises consistent readers.
Homework: read one page to a family member and retell it.
Encourage learners to borrow a book for the week.

competencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Communication and Collaboration; Creativity and Innovation; Personal Development and Leadership; Cultural Identity and Global Citizenship; Digital Literacy
resources: NaCCA approved textbook; TLMs; ICT tools; community resources
rpk: Learners speak the local language daily and built songs, reading, composition and grammar skills through Basic 1-4.
starter: Greet learners; 1-minute 'book talk': teacher shows and names a book from the class collection.
Quick recall: learners mention one thing they read last time.
NEW TODAY: Everyone reads Anansesɛm (folk tale book) quietly.
Set reading rules: eyes on text, quiet lips, note new words.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Silent reading – 7 min): Learners read Anansesɛm (folk tale book) individually; teacher listens to 2-3 learners read aloud in turn.
ACTIVITY 2 (Pair read – 5 min): Pairs take turns reading short passages aloud to each other; partners help with hard words.
ACTIVITY 3 (Respond to text – 5 min): Learners answer 3 quick questions: 'What was it about? Who was in it? Which part did you like?'
ACTIVITY 4 (Record – 3 min): Learners write the title and one sentence about Anansesɛm (folk tale book) in their reading log in the local language.
plenary: 2-3 learners share their favourite part with the class.
Teacher displays the reading log and praises consistent readers.
Homework: read one page to a family member and retell it.
Encourage learners to borrow a book for the week.
